title: You still need a liner!  This won't do the job alone
text:
You still need a liner! This won't do the job alone. Well, the mystery of how my daughter flooded our bathroom floor has been solved.

I bought this liner (clearly marked LINER, note) to go with a new fabric shower curtain
I had also purchased. Previously, we had just a vinyl curtain only. We have your basic bathtub - nothing
special or oversized, and we hung the liner and curtain like we always have.

First, the positives -
this curtain is beautiful - it really is. It has a light striped effect in shades of beige,
and it looks great on the hooks. It is very well made, and the weights in the bottom are exactly
what we had been looking for to keep the liner from billowing up and sticking to our soapy selves.
This is hanging on the INside of the tub, as liners should, with the new curtain on the outside of the tub.

After the first shower with the new curtains in place, we had a soaked floor, soaked rugs, etc.
We couldn't figure out what she did, and thought maybe water was hitting shampoo bottles and "leaking" out that way.
We even had blamed her for being careless with the handheld shower head.
Then I took a shower this morning.

I, too, had a flooded bathroom floor from a 10-12 minute shower. What the heck?!
I had made doubly sure that the corners/edges of the tub were covered with the liner.
Then I noticed what was really going on -

THIS LINER IS NOT WATERPROOF!
Nope - at least mine isn't!

This beautiful shower curtain "liner" should be considered a curtain ONLY.
It does not even repel water! It keeps shower spray in for a short while, but if water bounces off you and on to
the curtain, or you aim your shower head at the curtain to rinse off some soap, you will have
a soaked floor. This does NOT act like a liner at all, and in fact creates a wet mess.

Now, I know it said this was a fabric shower curtain liner, but wouldn't you think if it states
it is a LINER that it would be waterproof?!? I know I sure did! But it isn't.
At the end of my relatively short shower, my liner was soaked through, and had several places of
my new separate actual shower curtain soaked as well, and water puddled on the floor from where it dripped down
off the soaked fabric shower curtain. My rugs were soaked, as was a cardboard box of cat food packets I'd sat
on the floor, waiting to be put in the cupboard.

I've already discarded the packaging or I would return it. This is pitiful!
I like how the weights keep the curtain down in the tub, so my plan is to get a REAL liner that is
actually waterproof, and add it to the rings INBETWEEN the new curtain and this fabric liner.

Seriously - this was so disappointing! I really thought anything that called itself a liner
would act like one, but I was very wrong. I gave it two stars ONLY because it is very well made.

I would advise anyone thinking about getting this item (in any color) that they should consider it to be
ONLY a curtain, and to use a vinyl liner of some sort with it. It will keep someone from seeing you
"nekkid", but that is all it will do. It is not water repellant or water proof.

Just goes to show you that beauty does not mean brains - this looks a lot better than it works!
